transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-02 14:30 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (Redwood Product), Michael (Brightlane SRE), Sara (PM), Liam (Frontend), Olivia (Security)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood SDKs for Python and TypeScript, auth and env setup, Console quickstart, and Optimize recommendations for cost/latency. Agreed to start a short poc and run sample benchmarks.

00:00 Alex: alright good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, im joined by Priya who's our solutions engineer and Daniel on product side, how are we all doing?
00:12 Michael: good thanks, excited to see how the SDK fits into our stack, we have some latency constraints and also strict data residency so want to cover auth and private deployments.
00:22 Priya: great, we'll focus first on the local SDK quickstarts (python + ts), then show the console, then some Optimize tips around batching and quantization recs, sound good?
00:30 Sara: yep that's perfect, also can we keep a note of security questions for Olivia.
00:35 Olivia: thanks, i'll flag SOC2 + KMS questions but please call out SAML/SSO flow.
00:40 Alex: noted.
01:05 Priya: ok quick slide — the Redwood SDK is thin wrapper over the API, two packages: python package named "redwood" and npm package "@redwood/inference" in the quickstart we show pip install redwood and npm i @redwood/inference, sample code basically sets an env var REDWOOD_API_KEY or uses SSO token in private setups.
01:26 Liam: will the npm lib work in node and browser? we mostly run TS in Node 18 on lambda.
01:33 Priya: primarily node server-side is supported, browser usage is possible but we recommend proxying through your backend to keep keys safe. there is also a short-lived token flow for frontend but it's not generally recommended for production.
01:48 Michael: on env we want to confirm: do you support per-route keys or key-scoped roles? we need to separate dev/test keys from prod.
01:56 Alex: yes you can create scoped API keys in the Console and restrict them to models or routes, and Redwood Dedicated/Private supports VPC and customer-managed KMS.
02:10 Olivia: how does KMS actually integrate — is it bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM?
02:18 Priya: short answer yes — for Private we integrate with customer K M S and H S M options, and for Hosted we offer managed KMS but can rotate keys per account, we will send the security doc with integration details.
02:33 Daniel: also worth calling out audit logs (console->activity) tie back to requests and token usage for compliance audits.
02:42 Michael: good. ok let's go through a live code quickstart for Python.
02:50 Priya: copying the gist — in Python the example is:
	from redwood import RedwoodClient
	client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
	resp = client.generate(model='gpt-j-6b', prompt='summarize the following...')

03:18 Priya: note on models — we have a model catalog in the Console and the names can vary, quickstart picks a curated open model, but for prod you may want a specific quantized variant; we'll recommend per-workload model in the Optimize report.
03:36 Liam: ok about streaming — can we stream tokens in the Python lib? we need partial tokens to start rendering.
03:44 Priya: yes both SDKs support streaming. in python you can iterate over client.stream(...). there was a transcribe issue where a few token events sometimes batch — that's an edge in older clients, but the latest has continuous streaming support. we'll include code sample.
04:05 Sara: for the TS example?
04:07 Priya: TS is similar:
	import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'
	const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
	const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: [...] })

04:35 Liam: do you provide type definitions and examples for Next.js?
04:39 Priya: yes types included. for nextjs we recommend server-side calls from the API route. will share a small nextjs example.
04:47 Michael: let's talk auth flows briefly — we use Okta with SAML. how do we map SSO to Redwood Console roles?
04:55 Alex: Console supports SAML/SSO provisioning and SCIM, and you can map groups to RBAC roles. for API keys we still generate keys for service accounts; SSO is for users accessing console and managing keys.
05:12 Olivia: any caveats with audit trail when using SSO vs API keys? we need end-to-end evidence for requests.
05:20 Daniel: requests are logged with the acting principal and token id; for service account keys you'll see the key id in the audit log. SSO user actions appear by user id.
05:30 Michael: perfect.
05:50 Priya: switching to environment setup — for local dev we recommend: set REDWOOD_API_KEY in a .env file, pip install redwood, and run the quickstart. For staging and CI use pipeline secrets. For Dedicated/Private we provide a short-lived kube config for the private control plane or a VPN/peering setup if on VPC.
06:18 Liam: when you say private, is there a difference in the SDK usage? like different endpoints?
06:24 Priya: usually you point the SDK at your private endpoint (e.g., https://inference.mycompany.redwood.internal) and the auth flow is the same, pass API key or mTLS if you enable it. we'll include sample env var REDWOOD_BASE_URL in the quickstart.
06:42 Michael: about performance — can you show optimize recommendations for throughput?
06:48 Priya: yes Optimize gives batching and quantization suggestions based on workload. common recs: use prefix caching for chat bots, set max tokens conservatively, use 8-bit quantized model variants for throughput, and tune batch size to match your latency SLO. we have a sample benchmark script that emits concurrent requests and measures p95 token latency, we'll share that.
07:16 Sara: do you integrate with our datadog? we want traces and metrics.
07:20 Daniel: Console exposes per-route latency and token cost breakdown; we have integrations with prometheus and can forward metrics to Datadog — tracing hooks available via request headers so you can correlate.
07:32 Michael: on security: we'd want to restrict logs for PII, does Redwood mask or redact data?
07:38 Priya: we have configurable retention and redaction settings, plus option to disable retention for Dedicated/Private. we'll include the specific retention policies in the security doc.
07:50 Olivia: also need to confirm e2e encryption for streaming — is payload encrypted in transit?
07:56 Priya: yes TLS for all traffic, and you can enable mTLS on Private endpoints.
08:06 Alex: quick demo of Console — sharing screen (note: brief pause...)
08:35 Alex: Console -> Projects -> SDK Keys shows how to create scoped keys, here's the model selector and quickstart button that pre-populates a snippet, you can also pin model versions and set rollout policies.
09:02 Michael: can we set per-route quotas? we need rate-limit guardrails for bursty ML tasks.
09:08 Alex: yes per-key quotas and rate limits are supported and visible in the Console. also usage alerts can be configured.
09:18 Sara: about billing and cost visibility — if we run a poc what's the expected cost model?
09:24 Alex: hosted is usage-based per token, Dedicated is reserved capacity — for the poc we usually spin up a small sandbox on hosted but we can estimate token cost with sample workload. we'll follow up with a pricing estimate.
09:40 Liam: back to SDK integration specifics — do you support autopackaging models or do we handle serialization?
09:47 Priya: you push inputs via SDK, and Redwood handles tokenize/serialize. if you have custom tokenization needs we can surface hooks but generally not needed.
09:58 Michael: error handling strategy — how should we handle fallbacks?
10:03 Priya: standard pattern: retry with exponential backoff for 5xx, detect 429 and backoff, for capacity you can fallback to a cheaper model variant; the SDK surfaces status codes and headers with useful tokens. we'll provide an example middleware for retries in TS.
10:20 Alex: quick note: we occasionally have transcription glitches in calls — hope that doesnt confuse the notes :)
10:27 (laughter)
11:00 Priya: demo wrap-up — sending the quickstart code: Python gist shows env var, streaming example, and small benchmark; TS gist shows server-side sample, streaming + types.
11:25 Michael: can you also include a sample that shows how to enable prefix caching? we use a lot of repeated conversational context.
11:32 Priya: yes prefix and KV cache options are part of the request payload (cache_key, cache_ttl) and also via Console-level caching policies. we'll include the sample header and code snippet.
11:50 Olivia: one more security ask — can you show us a sample of the audit log entries we get for a request? even anonymized.
11:58 Daniel: will do, we'll redact IDs but show format.
12:10 Alex: ok to recap next steps — Alex will email the quickstarts, Priya shares sandbox creds and benchmark script, Daniel sends security + KMS docs, and schedule follow-up poc scoping for 6/9.
12:24 Michael: sounds good, thanks everyone.
12:28 Sara: thanks, very helpful.
12:30 Meeting ended.
